courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Movies and Politics
courses.description: Movies often reflect important social and political issues. In this course students will see a set of movies, discuss them, and put them into social and political contexts.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Friendship in Political Thought
courses.description: This seminar will explore what relationships have been designated "friendship" in the past, and why they are of such concern to political and ethical philosophers like Plato, Aristotle, Cicero, Montaigne, and Emerson. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Democratic Governance in Contemporary Latin America
courses.description: This seminar explores challenges in democratic governance in contemporary Latin America. With important regional variations, the exercise of state power reflects historical continuities of corruption, patronage politics, and other abuses of state resources. There are also demands for accountability and transparency across the region and more independent judiciaries.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Revolution, America in 1776 and France in 1789
courses.description: We examine the political theory of revolution at two dramatic moments in history: The American Revolution and The French Revolution. This course is throws students into New York City in 1775 and Paris in 1791 by recreating and engaging with the ideas and arguments of these times through two, role-immersive simulations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Social Movements and Political Protest and Violence
courses.description: Unconventional collective political behavior: mass movements, riots, demonstrations, revolts, and revolution.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The United States and the European Union: Partners or Rivals?
courses.description: The alliance between America and the European Union is one of the most important political relationships today.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Political Conflict in the European Union and the United States
courses.description: This course examines the politics of the European Union in comparison with the United States.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Entrepreneurship in Community and Economic Development
courses.description: This is a survey course of entrepreneurial strategies as they are used in community and economic development. It involves an individual research or service project by each student.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Introduction to Constitutional Conflicts
courses.description: This seminar will introduce students to the issues, arguments, history, impact, and reasoning arising from or in conflicts between presidents and Congress. The constitutional conflicts that are the focus of the course involve presidents and Congress fighting for primacy in areas in which they have shared constitutional powers.

source.text: POLI 74. | 3 Credits. | FY-SEMINAR, FC-KNOWING or FC-VALUES.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Thinking about Law
courses.description: This seminar explores the notion of a rule of law, statutory and case law, legal analysis, and the realities of the adversarial system and legal practice. Students will be engaged in analytical thinking and expression through classroom discussion, analytical papers, and examinations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Obama Presidency
courses.description: This course examines the presidency of Barack Obama, the first African American to serve in the nation's highest office.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Immigrants and Refugees in World Politics
courses.description: This class focuses on two different types of global migrants, immigrants and refugees, and explores why these two groups move out of their countries and how they are treated by receiving countries. Immigrants and refugees have traditionally been thought of as politically, legally, and ethically different from each other and this class explores these differences, but it also explores the many ways that they are similar.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: The Politics of Migration in Europe
courses.description: Europe is facing numerous complex issues ranging from economic uncertainty and rising populism to integrating migrants and respecting minority rights. A common thread running through these issues is the movement of people across national borders. This class examines how the movement of people into Europe and within Europe affects, and in turn is affected by, the politics in Europe, which are quite different from the politics in the United States. Drawing comparisons between Europe and the U.S. is an important feature of this class.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Global Politics of Climate Change
courses.description: Introduces politics of climate change policy at international, EU, US, state, and substate levels through readings, documentary films, and guest speakers.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: African-American Politics and Economic Inequality
courses.description: This course explores African-American political development from emancipation to the present, with a central focus on economic inequality. Special attention will be paid to the experiences and contributions of African-Americans in the struggle against economic inequality in the United States.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: First-Year Seminar: Special Topics
courses.description: Special topics course. Content will vary each semester.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Democracy in Changing Times
courses.description: Why do Americans love democracy, but hate politics? Why are there only two political parties? Why do voters hate, yet respond to negative campaigning? This course will introduce students to politics in the United States, addressing these and many more questions about how American democracy works. Honors version available.

source.text: POLI 100. | 3 Credits. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-VALUES, FAD.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Comparative Politics
courses.description: This course examines the diversity of political arrangements in societies across the globe. Honors version available.

source.text: POLI 130. | 3 Credits. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-GLOBAL.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations and Global Politics
courses.description: An introduction to the study of political and economic relations in the international system. Topics covered include international conflict, trade, global finance, international institutions, civil war, and human rights. Honors version available.

source.text: POLI 150. | 3 Credits. | FY-LAUNCH (only designated sections), FC-GLOBAL. | PWAD 150 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Relations and Global Politics Research Laboratory
courses.description: This laboratory section introduces students in POLI 150 to contemporary research methods in the study of international relations and world politics. Students will design and conduct independent research related to international politics. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Undergraduate Seminar
courses.description: A detailed examination of selected topics in the field of political science. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Internship in Political Science
courses.description: An opportunity to obtain credit for an internship in a government or public service organization. Pass/Fail only. Does not count toward the political science major. Requires permission of the department. Open to political science majors only.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, at least two POLI courses.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite, at least two POLI courses

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

source.text: POLI 193. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, at least two POLI courses. | HI-INTERN.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The President, Congress, and Public Policy
courses.description: An analysis of the roles and influence of the president, the Congress, and other participants in the making of national policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of Bureaucracy
courses.description: Problems of the public service; internal dynamics of public organizations; acquisition and allocation of public funds; the roles of bureaucracy in relation to public policy, clients, the citizenry, and society. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The United States Supreme Court
courses.description: Examination of the process of policy making on the Supreme Court. Focuses upon the selection of justices, factors affecting the court's decision making, and the impact of its policies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Innocence, and the Decline of the Death Penalty
courses.description: A large majority of Americans supports the death penalty in the abstract, but the number of death sentences and executions has been declining since the mid-1990s. This course explores the decline of the death penalty by looking at race, questions of innocence, and the new politics of capital punishment.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Southern Politics
courses.description: This course examines the politics of the American South. Each state is studied separately and we examine the region from a broad/general perspective. Both academic books and journal articles are read. By the end of the course, students should be familiar with historical and contemporary politics in the South.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics in the U.S. States
courses.description: State and local governments in the United States exercise considerable power over public policies such as education, social welfare, and taxation. This course examines similarities and differences across the U.S. states to better understand the causes and consequences of politics in these settings. Previously offered as POLI 101. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and the Right to Vote in the United States
courses.description: This course surveys scholarly literature on political psychology, electoral institutions, racial politics, and access to the ballot in the United States. In 30 hours of community service with partner organizations, students forge deeper connections between the university and the broader community. Through consistent reflections on the importance and potential downfalls of service learning, students gain a multi-faceted view of the practice and learn how to become better service learners.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Organized Interests
courses.description: This course examines how interests organize themselves, enter into and then interact within interest communities, and seek to influence government policy through electoral activity and lobbying legislators, executives, and courts.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Parties and Elections
courses.description: An analysis of the dynamics of party alignment and realignment and of nomination and election to public office in American national government. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analyzing Public Opinion
courses.description: A study of forces affecting public opinion and its expression in various political activities. Emphasis on gathering and analyzing opinion data. Course may be taught in the computer classroom. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Global Issues and Globalization
courses.description: Survey of international social, political, and cultural patterns in selected societies of Africa, Asia, America, and Europe, stressing comparative analysis of conflicts and change in different historical contexts. LAC recitation sections offered in French, German, and Spanish.

source.text: POLI 210I. | 3 Credits. | FC-GLOBAL or FC-POWER, INTERDISCI. | GLBL 210I , ANTH 210I , GEOG 210I , HIST 210I .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Religion and Politics
courses.description: Religion and politics are deeply intertwined in contemporary America, as evidenced by heated and often highly partisan debates over a wide variety of political issues such as abortion and immigration. This course addresses the variety of ways in which religion and politics intersect for voters and political elites with a focus on understanding how scholars operationalize religious concepts and use data to make empirical claims about the relationship between religion and politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Principles of Political Science
courses.description: Despite the appearance of complexity and randomness, politics is deeply structured in ways that can be researched and understood. This course has three objectives. First, it will provide students with essential nuts and bolts for further study in political science. Second, it introduces students who wish to study comparative politics and international organization to the substantive foundations of these fields. Third, and most generally, the course contributes to an understanding of global politics and varieties of democracy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Psychology: An Introduction
courses.description: Findings of the behavioral sciences are examined as they relate to politics. Includes such issues as human nature, community, political socialization, alienation, mass movements, belief systems, and personality.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Survey Research Methodology
courses.description: Surveys impact our lives in more ways than most people realize. Among other things, surveys allow us to predict who will win elections, determine how congressional districts are drawn, understand what the public wants from their elected leaders, and measure macroeconomic trends. This course examines how surveys are used in society, teaches students how to design and implement their own surveys, and provides training in how to analyze, interpret, and communicate survey findings to a broad audience.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, POLI 281 or equivalent, with instructor permission.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite, POLI 281 or equivalent, with instructor permission

source.text: POLI 216. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 281 or equivalent, with instructor permission. | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Women and Politics
courses.description: A comparison of men and women as political actors at the mass and elite level in America. Topics considered include the "gender gap," the women's movement, abortion, and the Equal Rights Amendment.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Electoral Representation in the United States
courses.description: This course examines the electoral representation of racial and ethnic minorities in the United States. While multiple ethnic groups are studied, there will be an emphasis on the two largest minority groups in the country: Latinos and African Americans.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Community Engaged Research
courses.description: This course introduces students to Community Engaged Research (CER), a research approach in which researchers directly engage and partner with community members throughout the research process, from developing questions to designing and conducting studies to produce rigorous academic research and build power for communities. The semester is divided into three modules. In the first module, students will learn the main pillars of CER. In the second module, students will apply the skills learned in the first module to major concepts in political science. The third module is dedicated to learning from community organizers and partners across a range of issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Latin America and the United States in World Politics
courses.description: A survey of the events, institutions, and issues that have dominated relations between Latin America and the United States.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of the United Kingdom
courses.description: An introduction to contemporary UK politics emphasizing the political battle between socialist and conservative ideologies. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Politics of the Middle East
courses.description: This course is designed as an introduction to contemporary Middle Eastern politics for advanced undergraduates. To explore this topic, the course combines systematic analytical approaches to big questions with concrete knowledge of events and developments in specific countries. In so doing, it aims to give students a critical understanding of politics while simultaneously building empirical knowledge about the Middle East/North Africa region. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Politics of the Global South
courses.description: An overview of politics and government in the Global South, emphasizing theories and challenges of development, modernization, and democratization. Regional emphasis may vary by instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Russia and Eurasia
courses.description: Factors and forces that explain the rise and demise of the Soviet political system and consideration of emerging new political configurations in the area. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of East-Central Europe
courses.description: Examines contemporary politics in east-central Europe by looking at the communist period, the 1989 revolutions, and the political, economic, and social transformations underway in the area. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of China
courses.description: An introduction to the politics of People's Republic of China with a focus on the Reform Era. Provides a working knowledge for understanding political events in contemporary China in three parts: historical background, evolution of political institutions, and changing relations between ordinary people and the Chinese state.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of the Global South: Latin America
courses.description: An introduction to politics and political economy of Latin America, emphasizing Latin America's position in the Global South and including consideration of leading theoretical explanations of development and political change. Country emphasis varies with instructor. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to European Government
courses.description: A treatment of the political institutions and processes of western European democracies, with special attention to France, Germany, England, and Italy. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: African American Politics
courses.description: A survey of African American political development from emancipation to the present. The course examines the dynamics of minority group politics with African Americans as the primary unit of analysis. Students consider African American politics in domestic and global contexts and issues of local, regional, national, and international relevance.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Political Behavior
courses.description: Political behavior is the study of attitudes, ideology, and engagement with the government. Why are some individuals more likely than others to support specific policies? How do we understand the connection between voters and political parties? What makes an individual more likely to vote? When and where are broad social movements, wars, rebellions and revolutions most likely to occur? Comparative political behavior studies how these phenomena operate across different institutional and cultural environments. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Intersectionality: Race, Gender, Sexuality, and Social Justice
courses.description: The first goal of this super course is to give students real tools for how to address multiple modes of difference and identity formations like race, gender, class, and sexuality.

source.text: POLI 248. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER. | AMST 248 , ENGL 248 , WGST 249 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Organizations and Global Issues
courses.description: Examines international organizations and their relationships with and impact upon international politics, international law, and selected global issues. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Problems in World Order
courses.description: An examination of selected topics in international relations, such as security and defense, international integration, and north-south relations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Environmental Politics
courses.description: Covers the politics of environmental issues, with a focus on issues that have become internationalized. It focuses on the special problems that arise in creating rules for environmental management and regulation when no single government has authority to enforce those rules.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Migration and Citizenship Today
courses.description: This class explores the moral, economic, political, and cultural dimensions of international migration. It is discussion-based and tackles such thorny questions as: Do we have an obligation to let poor people into our rich country? What constitutes persecution? How do foreigners affect national identity? How should citizenship be allocated? Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of the First Era (1880-1914) of Globalization
courses.description: This course considers the politics of international trade and finance on the eve of World War I. We explore the factors, domestic and international, that facilitated integration prior to World War I, as well as those that prevented a return to economic openness in the 1920s and 1930s.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics, Society, and Culture in Postwar Germany
courses.description: The interdisciplinary seminar will explore cultural, historical, and political issues of contemporary Germany and analyze German developments from the postwar period to the present. Readings and discussions in English.

source.text: POLI 257. | 3 Credits. | FC-PAST or FC-POWER. | HIST 257 , EURO 257 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of Migration and Mobility
courses.description: How does global migration affect both domestic and international political dynamics, and vice versa? This course explores the politics of global migration and mobility, offering insights into how the movement of people impacts politics at the individual, domestic, and international levels. Join the class to gain a deeper understanding of the migration issues shaping global discourses. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Crisis and Change in Russia and Eastern Europe
courses.description: Draws on historical, political, economic, and sociological perspectives to analyze social, cultural, and institutional change.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Feminism and Political Theory
courses.description: Introduction to feminist theory and its implications for the study and practice of political theory. Topics: women in feminist critiques of the Western political tradition, schools of feminist political theory.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Classical Political Thought
courses.description: Survey designed to introduce students to major political thinkers and ideas of the ancient world and of the medieval period. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Modern Political Thought
courses.description: Survey course designed to introduce students to major political thinkers and schools of thought dating roughly from the 16th century to the present. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Ethics of Peace, War, and Defense
courses.description: An analysis of ethical issues that arise in peace, war, and defense, e.g., the legitimacy of states, just war theory, terrorism, weapons of mass destruction.

source.text: POLI 272. | 3 Credits. | FC-POWER or FC-VALUES. | PHIL 272 , PWAD 272 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Nationalism, Immigration and the Politics of Identity
courses.description: Examination of the theories of nationalism and immigration, followed by an analysis of the interplay between national identity, immigration, and populism. This course first explores these issues theoretically and then more concretely by examining these issues in England and Scotland. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Major Issues in Political Theory
courses.description: An examination of major issues in political thought, including equality; obedience; violence and nonviolence; justice; forms of social, economic, and political life; liberty; and human nature and politics. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Political Thought Through the Civil War
courses.description: A survey course in early American political ideas through the Civil War, with emphasis on the role of politics, society, and economy in American thought. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Political Thought After the Civil War
courses.description: A survey course in American political ideas from the Civil War to the present, with emphasis on the role of politics, society, and economy in American thought. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Data in Politics I: An Introduction
courses.description: The Information Revolution has had a transformative effect on business, journalism, law, policy, and more. This course illustrates the breadth of ways in which data can help solve important social problems and increases students' comfort handling and analyzing data themselves. Students leave with a foundation for acquiring more advanced techniques.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Applied Experimental Research: Politics in the US and Europe
courses.description: The course familiarizes students with experimental research methods in political science, including laboratory experiments, field experiments, and survey experiments. Students will design and conduct an experimental research project on a research question about US or European politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Strategy and International Relations
courses.description: Introduction to the study of strategic decision making in international relations, with an emphasis on the application of basic game theoretic models. Incorporates in-class simulations of international relations scenarios.

source.text: POLI 287. | 3 Credits. | FC-KNOWING or FC-QUANT. | PWAD 287 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Strategy and Politics
courses.description: Offers an introduction to positive political theory, the application of rational choice analysis (or economic models) to the study of political phenomena. Topics include social choice theory, legislative voting, problems of cooperation and collective action, and public choice theory. Encourages students to think about politics from a critical vantage point.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science
courses.description: A detailed examination of special topics in political science. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Undergraduate Learning Assistant Practicum
courses.description: This course is for students selected as Undergraduate Learning Assistants (ULAs) for political science courses during the semester they serve as ULAs. This course will provide support and structure to make them effective in their role, including training in pedagogy and University policies; ongoing mentorship and supervision; and opportunities for reflection, assessment, and evaluation. May not count toward the political science major. Permission of the instructor.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 9 total credits. 9 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science, FC-POWER
courses.description: A detailed examination of special topics in political science.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Institute of Politics Fellows Seminar in Civic Leadership
courses.description: This course is facilitated by a Fellow from the UNC Institute of Politics, an experienced political practitioner who has held elected or appointed office. Over the course of the semester, students will engage in active and sustained dialogue with the Fellow and with one another on topics relevant to the Fellow's professional experience in public life. May not count toward the political science major.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and Public Policy in the United States
courses.description: Exploration of the relationship between race and public policy in the U.S. Primary focus on African Americans, but other racial groups also studied. Key areas include reproductive justice, health care, employment, labor, welfare, education, housing, environmental justice, policing, criminalization, foreign policy, immigration, and war.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Buying Influence: Interest Groups and Public Policy
courses.description: Students will gain an understanding of the role interest groups play in American public policy and how that role has shifted over time. The course emphasizes the role of interest groups in four policy areas: civil rights, the environment, social policy, and campaign finance.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Peace Science Research
courses.description: This Course-based Undergraduate Research Experience (CURE) introduces students to the practice of quantitative research on peace, conflict, and conflict resolution. Students work in teams to develop original research projects that answer policy-relevant questions in the field of peace science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Data in Politics II: Frontiers and Applications
courses.description: New approaches to data analysis are having a transformative effect on business, journalism, law, and policy - to name just a few sectors. This course is for students who have a basic familiarity working with social science data. It uses this foundation to teach more advanced ways to think about inference and uncertainty, with an emphasis on cutting-edge techniques and applications to real world problems.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Gateway to Philosophy, Politics, and Economics
courses.description: One course in economics strongly recommended. This interdisciplinary gateway course provides an introduction to subjects and quantitative techniques used to analyze problems in philosophy, political science, and economics. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Mentored Research in Political Science
courses.description: Required preparation, six hours of POLI course credit. Permission of the instructor. Students carry out a research project under the direct supervision of a faculty mentor. Learning contract required. Open to political science majors.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Readings in Political Science
courses.description: Required preparation, six hours of POLI course credit. Permission of the instructor. Directed readings in a special field under the direction of a faculty member. Learning contract required. Open to political science majors.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Executive Politics
courses.description: This course explores how presidents select policy options, how they decide timing, what shapes their congressional support, and how they build successful coalitions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy I: The Domestic System
courses.description: Problems of the national government in managing capitalist development and economic growth; political constraints; patterns of conflict among domestic actors.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Immigration, and Urban Politics
courses.description: This course provides a survey of the literature on race, immigration, and urban politics in the contemporary United States. The goal is to understand the complex relationship between racial/ethnic identity and local political processes. Students explore topics such as police brutality, immigration, the education system, and coalition politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Local Politics in the United States
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the politics of local governments in the United States. Topics covered include the economics and history of urban agglomerations, local governments' place in the American federal system, the role of race and immigration in how parties and coalitions govern, whether local governments are responsive to voters, and the role cities play in shaping housing, education, climate, and criminal justice policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: State Governments: Laboratories of Democracy
courses.description: Advanced topics in state government and politics, including political behavior and processes, governmental institutions, public policies. Emphasis on how states serve as the laboratories of democracy in a federal system.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Mock Constitutional Convention
courses.description: Students employ their understanding of political philosophy and practical politics to write a new constitution for the United States. Emphasis is on creative blending of theory and practice.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Constitutional Law I: Structures of Power
courses.description: A study of the U.S. Supreme Court's interpretation of the constitutional principles of federalism and the separation of powers. Focusing on the written opinions in the Court's leading cases, the course emphasizes both the legal and the political factors that shape the Court's constitutional decisions.

source.text: POLI 410. | 3 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, POLI 100 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Constitutional Law II: Civil Liberties and Rights
courses.description: A study of the U.S. Supreme Court's interpretation of the constitutional protections of the Bill of Rights and the Fourteenth Amendment. Relying upon the Court's written opinions in cases involving civil liberties and civil rights, the course examines how the Constitution limits the powers of both the federal and state governments. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: United States National Elections
courses.description: Course studies United States presidential and congressional elections. Emphasis on individual vote, changing party strengths, and the relation of outcomes to policy. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Election Administration in the United States
courses.description: This is a course about how we administer elections in the United States. The people, processes, and rules by which we administer elections in the United States are critically important to the exercise of free and fair elections that is a cornerstone of a democratic form of governance. A major component of this course is your work as an elections official in the Fall 2024 election. Must be a registered voter in Orange County, NC.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Constitutional Policies and the Judicial Process
courses.description: Analysis of the structure and functions of judicial systems emphasizing the organization, administration, and politics of judicial bureaucracies and roles of judges, juries, counsel, litigants, and interested groups in adjudication processes.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Political Psychology
courses.description: Examines in greater depth issues in the field of political psychology, including conflict and conflict resolution, socialization, attitude formation, mass movements, leader-follower relationships, and psychobiography. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Mass Media and American Politics
courses.description: Junior-senior standing required. Examination of the role, behavior, and influence of the mass media in American politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and Politics in the Contemporary United States
courses.description: Restricted to juniors and seniors. Surveys the vast literature on race and politics in the contemporary United States and examines the complex relationship between racial and ethnic identity and political outcomes. It explores broad political science concepts in the context of racial and ethnic groups. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Legislative Politics
courses.description: Examines the politics of the United States Congress. Emphasis on representation, the legislative process, and policy making. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Framing Public Policies
courses.description: This course will focus on the process by which policies get framed, or defined, in public discussions. Framing is focusing attention on some elements of a complex public problem rather than others. Readings combine psychological background with case histories of United States and comparative public policy changes over time.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Minority Representation in the American States
courses.description: This class explores the political representation of blacks, Latina/os, women, and gays and lesbians in the American states. How do these groups achieve descriptive and substantive representation? How does state context shape the political representation of these minorities? Students taking this course should have a strong interest in state politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Legislative Procedure in Congress
courses.description: Examines legislative procedure in Congress. Requires active participation in a Model Congress.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Sexuality, Race, and Gender: Identity and Political Representation
courses.description: Analyzing the impact of the descriptive representation of marginalized communities on public policy, legislation, and social change. Sexual orientation, identity, gender, ethnicity and race, and the intersectionality of these communities. We seek to understand the role that elected officials can have in driving change, affecting their colleagues and constituents.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Diversity and Politics
courses.description: Diversity is sometimes cited as a facilitator of political cooperation but more often it is considered a challenge for constructive civic engagement. This course engages the various ways in which different forms of diversity (e.g., racial, ethnic, religious, linguistic, national origin) and politics interact across a wide range of societies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analysis of National Security Policy
courses.description: Course explores contemporary threats to national security, approaches to national security strategy, policy instruments, the role of military force, and the policy-making process.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: African Politics
courses.description: This course explores the political and economic development of countries in sub-Saharan Africa, including historical factors and contemporary issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Tolerance in Liberal States
courses.description: Compares and explains contemporary cases of tolerance and intolerance in the U.S., Canada, and the EU. Considers controversies involving religion, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, political ideology, multiculturalism, and populism.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of the European Union
courses.description: Examines the politics and political economy of institutional change and policy making in the European Union in comparative perspective. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of Mexico
courses.description: This course provides a survey of 20th-century politics in Mexico, including the construction of the single-party regime under the PRI and the political and economic changes in the second half of the century that marked the end of the one-party regime and inaugurated a new era of political competition.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Democracy and Development in Latin America
courses.description: The analysis of central issues of democracy and development in Latin America. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Democracy and International Institutions in an Undivided Europe
courses.description: Explores the collapse of communist rule in 1989 and the reaction of international institutions to the challenges of democratization, economic transition, ethnic conflict, and European integration in an undivided Europe.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Analyzing European Public Opinion
courses.description: The course introduces students to the theory and practice of studying European public opinion. The course is split into four parts. In the first part, we will discuss core concepts and important problems in the study of public opinion. In the second part, we will study tools and common data sets for the analysis of European public opinion. In the third part, we will examine several recent contributions on different aspects of European public opinion.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: How to Stay in Power When the People Want You Dead: The Politics of Authoritarian Survival
courses.description: Dictators do not rely on consent of the people to stay in power. But they do still face constraints and must perform a delicate balancing act to maintain enough support to stay in office and reap its rewards. This class seeks to understand when autocrats are successful and when they fail.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Israeli Politics and Society
courses.description: This course will explore Israeli society, Israeli politics, and the Arab-Israeli conflict.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Political Economy
courses.description: Theories of international political economy, major trends in international economic relations, selected contemporary policy issues.

source.text: POLI 442. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 150 . | FC-GLOBAL. | EURO 442 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Foreign Policy: Formulation and Conduct
courses.description: The role of Congress, the press, public opinion, the president, the secretary and the Department of State, the military, and the intelligence community in making American foreign policy. Emphasizes the impact of the bureaucratic process on the content of foreign policy.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, POLI 150; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: POLI 443. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 150 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite. | PWAD 443 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Terrorism and International Peace
courses.description: The U.S. 9/11 attack represents the defining terrorist attack to Americans, but in most of the world, terrorism has long been part of politics. We will examine what motivates individuals to consider violence, how individuals organize to protect their political interests, the types of tactics used by violent groups and the state's response, before concluding with a study of collapsed states, the international implications of political violence, and possibilities for conflict resolution.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Immigrant Integration in Contemporary Western Europe
courses.description: Immigrant integration has been one of the most intense political issues in Western Europe in recent decades. The extent to which these immigrants have successfully integrated is a hot topic of debate across Europe, and there is no consensus about the best way to promote integration. This course explores these debates. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Multilevel Governance
courses.description: Political authority is changing around the world. Decision making has shifted down to state and local governments, such as Catalonia and Scotland, and up to international organizations such as the European Union and the World Health Organization. What does this mean for the future of the national state? Honors version available.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, At least one POLI course, EURO course, or TAM course.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite, At least one POLI course, EURO course, or TAM course

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Beg, Borrow, or Steal: How Governments Get Money and Its Effects on Accountability
courses.description: This course explores the politics behind taxation, foreign aid, natural resources, and debt, focusing on how each affects accountability and state capacity. Topics include when governments tax; whether taxation causes democratization; the effects of foreign aid and oil money on corruption and conflict; and how government debt shapes domestic politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Contemporary Inter-American Relations
courses.description: A comprehensive analysis of hemispheric international relations and foreign policies of individual Latin American nations. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Political Change in Comparative Perspective
courses.description: The course examines the interplay of race, ethnicity, political institutions, and political mobilization in modern state and nation-building. Through the use of broadly drawn international case studies, the politics of ethnicity and race is analyzed from the perspective of global processes of state building, colonialism and decolonization, and capitalist development as well from local development of ideology and political organizations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Africa and International Conflict
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to examine Africa's conflicts using an historical examination and advances in international relations theory. We will examine European colonial intervention, the wars of independence, the Cold War, and the use of proxies, insurgencies, the African World War, the Sudanese War, and the "war of terrorism."

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: When Countries Go Broke: Political Responses to Financial Crises
courses.description: What happens when countries go broke? This course considers the complex historical relation between revenue generation and the development of the nation-state, and details a variety of major crises facing governments today, including the political determinants of and responses to major recent financial crises.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Conflict Processes
courses.description: Analysis of international conflict and the causal mechanisms that drive or prevent conflict. Emphasis is on the conditions and processes of conflict and cooperation between nations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Conflict Management and Resolution
courses.description: Examines the management and resolution of international and civil wars. Honors version available.

source.text: POLI 458. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 150 . | RESEARCH. | PWAD 458 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Trans-Atlantic Security
courses.description: The course explores the development of Euro-Atlantic security institutions (NATO, EU) and compares security policy in the United States and Europe. Cases include policy toward the Balkans, Afghanistan, Russia, and Ukraine. Includes review of concepts of security and selected international relations approaches to international organizations. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Polarization and Partnership: American Politics and Transatlantic Relations
courses.description: This course examines how polarization in U.S. politics shapes the evolving partnership between America and Europe. It explores how partisan conflict, populism, and institutional fragmentation influence transatlantic cooperation on climate policy, energy security, technology regulation, and defense. Combining perspectives from comparative and international politics, students analyze the tensions and opportunities defining contemporary transatlantic relations. Through theory-driven readings, discussions, and a final individual research paper, the course encourages critical reflection on how domestic divides and global uncertainty affect multilateral cooperation, trust, and the future of the transatlantic alliance.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: A Divided Union? Polarization of Climate Change in the EU
courses.description: This course examines how polarization and public opinion shape climate policy within the European Union. Focusing on fragmentation across member states, it analyzes how national preferences and contestation influence EU-wide ambition and governance. Students will critically assess institutional responses, the EU's leadership in global climate politics, and the challenges of sustaining collective action. Through country-specific case studies, progress reports, and an independent term paper, students explore the political dynamics that determine the EU's ability to act as a global environmental leader amid deepening societal and ideological divides.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Conflict and Intervention in the Former Yugoslavia
courses.description: Focuses on ethnic and political conflicts in the former Yugoslavia and efforts by the international community to end conflict and promote peace and reconstruction. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Social and Political Philosophy
courses.description: An examination of the logic of social and political thought with an analysis of such concepts as society, state, power, authority, freedom, social and political obligation, law, rights. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Contemporary Political Thought
courses.description: Survey of the historical foundations, central tenets, and political consequences of prominent 20th-century political theories. Topics include contemporary liberalism and Marxism, fascism, theories of development, populism, feminism. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Problems of Modern Democratic Theory
courses.description: Major problem areas in democratic theory including definitions, presuppositions, and justifications of democracy, liberty, equality, minority rights, public interest, participation, dissent, and civil disobedience. Honors version available.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics and Literature
courses.description: Identifies and interprets political ideas using historical and contemporary literary sources. Examines literature as political practice.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Global Justice
courses.description: This course looks at major themes in contemporary theories of global ethics and global justice. Potential topics include the duty to give aid to foreigners, global distributive justice, resource rights and justice, and immigration ethics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Environmental Political Theory
courses.description: This course brings the tools and techniques of political theory to bear on contemporary environmental challenges. Students will examine different conceptions of nature and of human-nature relations, investigate arguments about the moral and political status of nonhuman others, think about the role of individual responsibility in addressing climate change, and grapple with issues of inequality, environmental justice, and power.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Political Theory of the American Founding
courses.description: A role-immersive simulation of the Constitutional Convention of 1787. Students employ their knowledge of the political theory and science of the founding period to become the Convention of 1787 and write a constitution.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: Examines in greater depth and complexity current issues in feminist political theory. Topics: theories of subjectivity and solidarity, feminist poststructuralist and post-Marxist thinking, gender in the public sphere.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics, Philosophy, and Economics of Education
courses.description: The course explores the politics, philosophy, and economics of US education. We will cover topics such as the goals of education; education politics at the local, state, and federal levels; school finance; accountability; markets in education; the role of philanthropy; and student debt.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Survey Experiments
courses.description: A research intensive course on the design, implementation, interpretation, and communication of political science survey experiments. Honors version available.

source.text: POLI 480. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 281 or equivalent. | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Understanding Influence: Misinformation, Polarization, and Social Media in Politics
courses.description: This course is designed to provide a broad introduction to key questions, theories, methodologies, and debates in public opinion, with an emphasis on cutting edge research in the current public opinion literature on the topic of misinformation, polarization, and social media. How informed is the public? How does the public need to be? What are the cognitive and social origins of misinformation? Why has polarization increased so dramatically over the past 40 years? What role does social media, and the internet more generally, play in democratic societies in the 21st century?
