courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Networks in International Relations
courses.description: The modern international system is a highly-connected interdependent network of people, non-state actors, and governments. The course will introduce key concepts from network analysis to provide the conceptual and methodological tools to analyze networks in international politics. Students will also learn statistical tools used to analyze and visualize network data.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: Increasingly, political and social scientists are using game theory to analyze strategic interactions across different settings. This course aims to give students a deep technical understanding of the most relevant concepts of game theory and how these concepts have been applied to the study of political and economic phenomena.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Special Topics in Political Science
courses.description: A detailed examination of advanced special topics in political science. Honors version available.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 12 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Contestation in Europe
courses.description: Examines recent developments in the European integration process by exploring the potential for political contestation concerning European Union matters in national politics. Familiarizes students with the main theoretical approaches and the extensive empirical work dealing with the effects of European integration.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: European Security: The Enlarging European Union and the Trans-Atlantic Relationship
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. Since the collapse of communism from 1989 to 1991, the European Union has faced a fundamentally different geopolitical neighborhood and an evolving relationship with the United States. We will explore how Europe has addressed new challenges to its security in its neighborhood and beyond.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The European Union as a Global Actor
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for undergraduates. This seminar introduces students to basic theoretical approaches to both international relations and the European Union by focusing on the European Union's external relations and foreign policies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Transatlantic Politics of Climate Change
courses.description: This course compares climate change policies of the European Union and the United States within the context of global climate policy and institutions. By investigating climate change policy, students will gain an understanding of the policy processes in the EU and US. The course also introduces climate policy in EU member states and US states. Students engage in active learning exercises and produce a final research paper.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: EU Foreign Policy in Times of Uncertainty
courses.description: This research-intensive seminar examines the evolution of EU foreign policy amid growing global uncertainty and internal contestation. Organized around thematic modules, the course explores how the EU navigates key domains--security, climate, trade, migration, and digital governance--while balancing normative commitments and strategic interests. Students engage critically with challenges such as de-Europeanization, norm contestation, and polarization, analyzing how external shocks like Russia's invasion of Ukraine reshape policy responses. Combining theory-driven scholarship with official EU sources, the course culminates in an individual term paper and includes a Diplomacy Lab component on Arctic security and EU-U.S. coordination.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Honors Seminar in Research Design
courses.description: Required of all students in the honors program in political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research
courses.description: Required of all students in the honors program in political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Honors Thesis Research
courses.description: Required of all students in the honors program in political science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Philosophy, Politics, and Economics: Capstone Course
courses.description: Permission of the department. The Capstone Seminar is the final course in the PPE sequence. The seminar has two components: a set of readings that focus on cutting edge work at the intersection of Philosophy, Political Science, and Economics and individual research projects selected in consultation with the instructor. The project involves giving a presentation to, and getting feedback from, seminar participants, and culminates in a final research paper. Throughout, participants will be actively engaging with each other, deepening their understanding of core concepts and tools of PPE, and applying them to specific issues.

source.text: POLI 698. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, PHIL 384 . | FC-VALUES. | PHIL 698 , ECON 698 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Core Seminar on American Political Institutions
courses.description: An overview of research on American politics that introduces students to a wide range of substantive understandings and theoretical perspectives. POLI 700 emphasizes American political institutions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Core Seminar on American Political Behavior
courses.description: An overview of research on American politics that introduces students to a wide range of substantive understandings and theoretical perspectives. POLI701 emphasizes mass political behavior.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Congress and Theory Building
courses.description: This course examines diverse theoretical perspectives on national institutional change and stability, using as our institutional focus the United States Congress between 1789 and 1989.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Presidency
courses.description: Survey of the substantial literature and research on the American Presidency.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Judicial Politics
courses.description: Survey of recent literature on the politics of judicial institutions and the behavior of judges, lawyers, litigants, and other actors in the judicial process, emphasizing relationships between judicial and other policy-making processes.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Race and Politics in the United States
courses.description: Race is at the center of American politics. Everything from voting rights to education policy to the quality of drinking water is shaped by race. This graduate seminar will focus on race in US politics, and while readings will cover multiple racial groups, Black politics will receive the most attention. My goal is that you will leave this course with a broad understanding of how central race is to understanding American politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar in Subnational Politics and Policy
courses.description: This course surveys the major topics and research programs in subnational American politics and policy, with special attention to the vertical and horizontal intergovernmental interactions inherent within federal political systems.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Parties
courses.description: Selected problems and issues in the study of American and comparative parties and party systems.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Current Research on Mass Political Behavior
courses.description: Theoretical study of mass behavior (i.e., participation, voting, protest) in the American context. This course emphasizes recent research.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Public Opinion
courses.description: A study of public opinion, its formation, expression, and impact on political systems and public policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Dynamics of Electoral Politics
courses.description: Change within mass electorates. Topics include issue and attitude change, political realignments, and models of electoral competition.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Socialization
courses.description: The learning process by which individuals acquire values, attitudes, and norms affecting their behavior in the political community, with emphasis on major agencies of socialization: family, schools, peer groups, and media.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar on Political Psychology
courses.description: This course surveys and evaluates current and past research in political psychology. Topics may include: personality, attitudes and values, socialization, political reasoning, information processing, decision making, political identity, and political affect.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Organized Interests in United States Politics
courses.description: The course examines the major theories and empirical research on how organized interests mobilize and maintain themselves, interact within populations, exercise influence through lobbying, and impact public policy. It includes the full range of interest organizations operating in American politics at any level and in all institutional venues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Potential for Democratic Stability in Deeply Divided Societies
courses.description: The theory of power sharing tries to explain how stable democracy is possible in deeply divided societies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Agenda-Setting
courses.description: This class will focus on theoretical and empirical approaches to the study of agenda-setting in both American and comparative settings. Begins in the 1950s through current literature, covering a wide range of methodological approaches. Assignments include participation in seminar discussion, short papers on readings, and substantial original research paper.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Managing Public Policy
courses.description: The role(s), function(s), and strategy of public administrators in the formulation, adoption, and implementation of public policies. Policy from the perspective of the policy maker; cases exploring the relationship of theories to actual policy processes. Spring.

source.text: POLI 720. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, POLI 700 , 745 , or PUBA 723 .

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Public Policy and Administration
courses.description: Alternative explanation of public policies and policy-making processes; introduction to policy analysis as a way to inform choices among policy options; policy implementation through administrative practices and procedures.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Approaches to Conflict Transformation: Theory and Practice of Peacebuilding Across Contexts
courses.description: In this course, students will learn about a variety of mechanisms for resolving or transforming conflict on interpersonal, community, state, and international levels. The pedagogy of this course will be both theoretical and practical. Through readings, assignments, and class discussion, we will wrestle with questions about the efficacy, significance, and ethical implications of various methods of conflict transformation; and we will learn some techniques of conflict resolution from experienced practitioners.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Organization Design
courses.description: Field theory, motivation, communication, and systems perspectives as theoretical bases for organization design.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, POLI 700, or permission of the instructor.

source.text: POLI 724. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 700 , or permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Public Administration Analysis and Evaluation II
courses.description: Second course in a two-course sequence introducing students to applied research design, data collection, data management, data analysis, and analytical reporting to allow students to conduct original research, be informed consumers of other research, and ultimately improve public program planning and evaluation decisions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Intergovernmental Relations
courses.description: Conflict and cooperation among governmental officials representing national, state, and local governments in the United States; changing roles of governments and new mechanisms for intergovernmental collaboration.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Framing
courses.description: This class will focus on the theoretical and empirical studies of individual and collective framing. Readings will be from journalism, sociology, psychology, and political science and will include both US-based and comparative studies. Assignments include participation in seminar discussion, short papers on readings, and substantial original research paper.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Policy Workshop
courses.description: Application of theories and techniques of policy analysis and planning to current public problems for actual clients. Focus on design and execution of policy research, and interpretation and presentation of results.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Psychology of Collective Politics
courses.description: Explores the psychological underpinnings of collective politics from the perspective of both individuals and groups. Political behaviors examined include deliberation, protest, nationalism, and intergroup conflict.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Political Research and Analysis
courses.description: The seminar introduces the beginning graduate student to the central issues and major developments in the field of comparative government and politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Politics of Development and Change
courses.description: The theories, concepts, and mechanisms of political change, with particular attention to processes of development and modernization in the new nations of Africa, Asia, and Latin America.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of Multilevel Government
courses.description: The vertical distribution of governmental authority is changing around the world. Decision making, resources, and power are shifting downward (to state and local governments) and upward (to supra-national bodies like the European Union, other regional or international organizations). This course examines theories and empirical studies that explore the causes and consequences of these trends.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: European Institutions and Integration
courses.description: This seminar introduces students to key concepts and developments of European integration and critically assesses the evolution of the European Union.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Political Behavior
courses.description: Political behavior of the public in cross-national or non-American settings. Political culture, belief systems, participation, protest, revolution, voting behavior, civic behavior, socialization, and media.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Bureaucracy
courses.description: A cross-national examination of functions, career patterns, role behavior, and relationships of bureaucratic elites within the context of national political systems. Research on particular countries is emphasized.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Transitions and Democratization in Comparative Perspective
courses.description: Examination of contrasting theoretical approaches to understanding democracy. Comparative study of Africa, Eastern Europe, and Latin America elucidates challenges and opportunities that affect possibilities for democratization and consolidation.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Psychology of Elite Decision Making
courses.description: Political thinking of politicians and civil servants in domestic and foreign policy. Perception, cognition, learning, attitude change and persuasion, aging, motivation, emotions, and personality.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Power and Morality in Politics
courses.description: Motives of power and morality in rational choice theories and theories of power sharing. Empirical findings and normative evaluations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Communist Political Systems
courses.description: An examination of the political evolution and process in societies governed by communist parties.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Issues in Latin American Politics
courses.description: Explores the central issues of Latin American politics and analyzes major theoretical debates.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Latin American Politics: Research and Analysis
courses.description: Reviews major works and theoretical perspectives in the literature, assesses contemporary political science research on Latin America, and examines problems of field research.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of Latin American Development
courses.description: Examines effects of state, regime-type, and political processes on agricultural and industrial policy in Latin America. Also considers the informal economy, international debt, and relationship between policy and politicization.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar on United States - Latin American Relations
courses.description: Analysis of the central conceptual concerns and major theoretical approaches to the study of inter-American relations, with a focus on United States foreign policy toward the region.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: African Politics: Challenges of Democratization and Development
courses.description: Study of the politics of development in contemporary Africa, with emphasis on changing state society relations, the roles of peasants and women in politics, and prospects for democratization.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Varieties of Democratic Capitalism in Europe and North America
courses.description: This course will examine the development of different types of welfare states in Europe and North America.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Identities and Transitions
courses.description: Capstone course for the REEES concentration in the Global Studies MA program. Interdisciplinary course focusing on the variety of problems encountered by the societies of East European countries and successor states of the former Soviet Union in their transition from communism to democracy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Diversity and Politics
courses.description: Diversity is sometimes cited as a facilitator of political cooperation but more often it is considered a challenge for constructive civic engagement. This course engages the ways in which different forms of diversity (e.g., racial, ethnic, religious, linguistic, gender, national-origin, sexuality) and politics interact across a wide range of societies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Fiscal Politics
courses.description: This course covers the politics of government budgets. It focuses on the sources of revenue (taxation, foreign aid, national resources, and debt) as well as levels of redistribution in a comparative perspective.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Theories of International Relations I
courses.description: Introduction to the central issues and major theoretical developments in the field of international relations, focusing on system structure, political and security issues, and decision making.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Theories of International Relations II
courses.description: Introduction to the central issues and major theoretical developments in the field of international relations, focusing on the politics of international economic relations, law and organization, and fundamental system change.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Organization
courses.description: Theories and approaches to the study of international organizations and regimes, plus selected noneconomic case studies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: International Conflict and Cooperation
courses.description: An examination of international conflict and cooperative processes in the context of the evolution of the international system.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Formal Models of International Relations
courses.description: An examination of research that uses formal models to analyze decision making in international relations, with a focus on non-cooperative game theory.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Politics of the International Economy
courses.description: Positive theories of political choice in trade, monetary relations, foreign investment, and regional integration.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of the Nation State in the World System
courses.description: Analysis of the interaction between the external sector of the economy and domestic politics in weak capitalist states.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, ECON 460 or 465; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: POLI 757. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, ECON 460 or 465 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Theories of Foreign Policy
courses.description: This course is an introduction to the field of foreign policy analysis. Its primary goal is to expose students to the theories and methods of foreign policy research and analysis.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research in Cooperation and Conflict Processes
courses.description: Advanced doctoral-level course. Builds off POLI 750 to explore current lines of research on conflict and cooperation. Each student will develop potential research projects and one expanded research project. The project should be suitable for subsequent development into a thesis and/or publication. Course focuses on research and the research process.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Divided Societies
courses.description: When a society is deeply divided along racial, ethnic, religious or linguistic lines, this classical model brings the risk that the majoritarian segment of society always stays in power.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Feminist Political Theory
courses.description: A survey of feminist approaches to politics and political inquiry.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Modern Political Theory
courses.description: An introduction to modern political thought, its major thinkers and issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Major Issues in Political Theory
courses.description: An introduction to the major issues of political theory, with emphasis on the major thinkers in the history of Western political thought.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Classical Political Theory
courses.description: An introduction to ancient and medieval political thought, its major thinkers and issues.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: American Political Theory
courses.description: Survey of issues and problems in American political thought, with analysis of major thinkers and selected topics and emphasis on the role of family, society, and economy in political theory.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Recent and Contemporary Political Theory
courses.description: An introduction to recent and contemporary political thought, its major thinkers and issues. Emphasis on Continental thought.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Major Figures in Political Theory
courses.description: An in-depth study of the primary and secondary literature on one or two major figures in the history of political thought (e.g., Plato, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Marx).

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: The Formal Theory of Institutions
courses.description: This course is a comprehensive introduction to the burgeoning literature on the formal theory of institutions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Scope and Methods of Political Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. A discussion of the theory and process of political analysis, including philosophy of science, research design, the methods of drawing causal inferences, and of generating data.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Logic of Political Inquiry
courses.description: A critical examination of models of political inquiry. Empirical (naturalist), interpretive, and critical metatheories are considered in terms of each model's ontological, epistemological, and practical/political consequences and presuppositions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Probability and Statistics
courses.description: Introduction to probability theory and basic principles of statistical inference, including estimation and tests of hypotheses; basic programming in R.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Methods for Causal Inference
courses.description: Introduction to causal inference techniques, with an emphasis on applications in Political Science and other Social Sciences. The course adopts a design-based perspective, clearly differentiating between identification assumptions which guide the treatment assignment process and the probabilistic models that generate outcomes. After defining frameworks based on potential outcomes and causal graphs, we focus on techniques for designing and analyzing experimental and observational studies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Time Series Analysis of Political Data
courses.description: Discusses the problems that arise when regression methodologies are applied to time series and pooled time series data.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, POLI 784; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite

source.text: POLI 786. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, POLI 784 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Advanced Topics in Political Data Science
courses.description: Survey of important contemporary trends in advanced data analysis. Likely topics include multilevel models, measurement models, machine learning, modeling dependence, and advanced computation in R.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Statistics and Data Analysis for Political Science and Policy Research
courses.description: This course focuses on the application of statistical analysis to quantitative data in order to study theoretically and substantively interesting questions about politics and policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Game Theory
courses.description: This class provides graduate students with an introduction to game theoretic modeling, focusing on noncooperative game theory. Topics covered include normal form games, extensive-form games, and games of incomplete information.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Positive Political Theory
courses.description: This seminar surveys applications of rational choice models across the subfields of political science. It also considers critiques of national choice approaches and alternative theoretical approaches to modeling human behavior.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Game Theory II
courses.description: This course is designed for students who desire greater proficiency in the more advanced topics. The course focuses on games of incomplete information that are widely used in political science like signaling and cheap-talk games and on topics that are starting to play a prominent role like principal agents models.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Research Seminar in Political Communication
courses.description: Participants consider the scientific literature and conduct innovative research. Topics focus on different media institutions' structure, political actors' communication strategies, and the ways that citizens engage with social, print, and electronic media. The aim is to better understand political news, public opinion, and the character of electoral democracy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: TAM Internship Credit
courses.description: POLI 799 includes both an internship and an academic component. The student intern is required to work at least 8 hours per week, for a minimum of 100 hours, at the internship agency. In addition to the hours worked, the student must, under the supervision of the faculty supervisor, write a research paper or complete a comparable project, and keep a journal of internship activities.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, one semester of coursework in TAM.

prerequisites.text: Prerequisite, one semester of coursework in TAM

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar on Application of Political Behavior Research to Public Problems
courses.description: Exploration and examination of the ways in which political behavior research can be applied to understanding and ameliorating public problems.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar in Political Sociology
courses.description: The relationships between social structure and political decisions. Regimes and social structure; bureaucracies, political associations, and professions; science and politics; closed and open politics; political movements and change.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative Welfare States
courses.description: This course examines the development, achievements, present crisis, and future of welfare states in advanced industrial democracies.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: European Politics
courses.description: Active participation of students in a research project on career motives and ethical principles in European countries.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Comparative European Societies
courses.description: Examination of commonalities and differences of European societies and of the tensions and difficulties attending the European integration process.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar in International Communication
courses.description: Reading and research in selected topics. Focus in recent years has included global news flow, communication and social change, communication in the collapse of communism, Western dominance in international communication, global culture, and the influence of technology.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisite, MEJO 446; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisite.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Theories of International Politics
courses.description: Topics relating to the development of theory in the realm of international politics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar in International Relations
courses.description: Special topics in international relations, such as alliances, bargaining, decision making, economic interdependence, and international human rights.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: U.S.-E.U. Lecture Series
courses.description: One credit course designed to enhance students' understanding of transatlantic studies through lectures from and discussion with experts in the field. Topics will focus on European Union and/or United States foreign and domestic politics as well as on contemporary transatlantic relations.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Political Economy of International Money and Finance
courses.description: Investigates the linkages between politics and economics in various realms of global finance, including exchange rates, sovereign debt, and foreign direct investment. Consider efforts to govern global finance, as well as the intersections between domestic politics and the international economy. Classical works and recent research in this area.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Data Collection Methods
courses.description: Reviews alternative data collection techniques used in surveys, concentrating on the impact these techniques have on the quality of survey data. Topics covered include errors associated with nonresponse, interviewing, and data processing.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Questionnaire Design
courses.description: Examines the stages of questionnaire design including developmental interviewing, question writing, question evaluation, pretesting, questionnaire ordering, and formatting. Reviews the literature on questionnaire construction. Provides hands-on experience in developing questionnaires.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Practicum on Experiments in Political Science
courses.description: A practicum on conducting experiments in Political Science.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Seminar in Political Theory
courses.description: Special topics in political theory such as Marxism and Socialism, Democratic theory, contemporary political thought, or related topics.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Design and Analysis of Experiments and Surveys
courses.description: Introduction to the use of experimental and survey research methods in political science. Topics include: factorial designs, repeated measures design, ANOVA, sampling theory, survey errors and costs, and questionnaire design.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Teaching Political Science
courses.description: This course is designed to train graduate students to serve as teaching assistants. It will focus on how to teach at UNC and how to run a good section. Topics covered will include rules and regulations, resources available through student services, emergency procedures, classroom management, how to stimulate discussion and keep up participation, and how to develop supplementary syllabi.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Fall Friday Lecture Series on Trans-Atlantic Topics
courses.description: This course is designed to enhance students' understanding of trans-Atlantic studies through lectures from and discussion with experts in the field.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Bayesian Modeling for Political & Social Research
courses.description: Introduction to Bayesian modeling and data analysis. The course focuses on basic Bayesian and MCMC theory, as well as applications in the context of common regression and measurement models, including multilevel (generalized) linear models, mixture models, item-response theory models and models for text classification. Basic knowledge of mathematical statistics is desirable, and working knowledge of both the R programming language and the maximum likelihood estimation framework is required.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
courses.description: A seminar-style course providing an introduction to the main concepts and models of machine learning. Prior completion of POLI 883 is recommended.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Behavioral Economics and Experiments
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to provide students with an introduction to behavioral decision research and its applications. Behavioral decision research is intensely interdisciplinary, employing concepts and tools from economics, statistics, and other disciplines, as well as the core discipline of psychology. BDR has had an impact on the fields of medicine, law, military science, environmental sciences, and public policy.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Applying Data Analysis to Transatlantic Studies
courses.description: This course is designed to get students to expand multivariate data analysis skills and to think critically about the presentation of information in professional settings and the media. A key goal is to give participants the confidence to critically evaluate whether the presentation of data is professionally sound. Another central goal is to expand skills in multivariate analysis by engaging in a semester-long research project that culminates in a publication quality paper.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Directed Readings in Political Science
courses.description: Permission of the department. Directed readings in a special field under the direction of a member of the graduate faculty.

courses.subject: POLI
courses.title: Special Topics in Political Science
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Seminar in selected areas of political science. Topics vary from year to year. May be repeated for credit.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.
